lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 6, when is A AND B true? (Only when A and B are both true.) Today: logic gates, the tiny circuits that do this inside every processor.
A logic gate takes inputs of 1 (on, true) or 0 (off, false) and gives an output. AND gives 1 only when both inputs are 1. OR gives 1 when either is 1. NOT flips its input.
A truth table lists every set of inputs and the output. With 2 inputs it has 4 rows; with 3 inputs, 8. Each extra input doubles the rows.
Gates join into circuits: one gate's output becomes another's input. Work from the inputs to the lamp, one gate at a time.
Worked example: a safe opens when (the key is in AND the code is right) OR the manager presses the override. With key 1, code 0 and override 1: AND gives 0, then OR gives 1, so it opens.
Inside a processor, billions of tiny transistors make gates, and gates that add binary numbers make the ALU. Claude Shannon (1916-2001) showed in 1937 how circuits of switches can do logic.
Gates are all around: a car alarm sounds when it is set AND a door opens. A lift moves only when its door is shut AND a button is pressed. A hall light comes on from either switch: OR.
Try it in the world: in the game, put a lamp between two levers. Either lever lights it, like an OR gate. Two switches one after the other on a real wire make AND. Next: databases.

exercises.hint: AND needs both inputs to be 1.
exercises.explain: A = 1 and B = 1, so AND gives 1 and the lamp lights.

exercises.prompt: OR gives 1 when either input is 1.
exercises.hint: Say the rule for OR in words.
exercises.explain: True: OR gives 1 if A is 1, if B is 1, or if both are.

exercises.prompt: How many rows does a truth table for 2 inputs have?
exercises.hint: List the ways two 0s and 1s can be set.

exercises.prompt: Match each gate to its rule.
exercises.hint: Say each gate's name as a sentence about its inputs.
exercises.explain: AND needs both, OR needs either, and NOT gives the opposite of its input.

exercises.hint: NOT gives the opposite of its input.
exercises.explain: The input A is 1, and NOT flips it to 0.

exercises.hint: Work out OR and NOT first, then AND.
exercises.explain: A OR B = 0 OR 1 = 1; NOT C = NOT 0 = 1; and 1 AND 1 = 1, so it lights.

exercises.prompt: A circuit has three inputs: A, B and C. How many rows does its truth table need?
exercises.hint: Each extra input doubles the rows.
exercises.explain: 2 inputs need 4 rows, so 3 inputs need 4 × 2 = 8 rows.

exercises.prompt: Does A AND B give 1 or 0?
exercises.hint: AND needs both inputs to be 1.
exercises.explain: Only A = 1, B = 1 gives 1; every other row gives 0.

exercises.hint: Work out the AND gate first, then the OR.
exercises.explain: True: A AND B = 1 AND 0 = 0, then 0 OR C = 0 OR 1 = 1.

exercises.prompt: Order the steps to work out a circuit's output.
items: feed its output into the next gate
exercises.hint: Start at the inputs, finish at the lamp.
exercises.explain: Inputs first, then each gate in turn from left to right, then the lamp shows the output.

exercises.prompt: In the truth table for A OR B, how many of the 4 rows give 1?
exercises.hint: Which row has neither input on?
exercises.explain: Only 0 OR 0 gives 0, so 3 of the 4 rows give 1.

exercises.hint: Work from the inputs: the NOT on B first.
exercises.explain: NOT B = NOT 1 = 0; A OR 0 = 0 OR 0 = 0; NOT 0 = 1, so the lamp lights.

exercises.prompt: An alarm's circuit has 5 sensors as its inputs. How many rows does its full truth table have?
exercises.hint: Double the rows for each extra input.

exercises.prompt: A lift moves when its door is shut and a floor button is pressed. Which logic fits?
exercises.hint: Must both be true, or is one enough?
exercises.explain: The lift needs both at once: door shut AND button pressed.

exercises.prompt: A security light: (dark AND movement) OR the test button. On or off?
exercises.hint: Check the AND part first, then the OR.
exercises.explain: It is on when it is dark with movement, or when the test button is pressed; otherwise it is off.

exercises.prompt: NOT (A AND B) gives 0 only when A and B are both 1.
exercises.hint: Work out A AND B for each row, then flip it.
exercises.explain: True: A AND B is 1 only for 1 and 1; NOT flips that to 0, and every other row to 1.

exercises.prompt: In the truth table for A AND B AND C, how many of the 8 rows give 1?
exercises.explain: Only A = 1, B = 1, C = 1 gives 1: 1 row of 8.
